newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Liechtenstein says it would not allow Mobutu in.
newsitem.headline: Liechtenstein says it would not allow Mobutu in.

text.p: Liechtenstein does not want deposed Zairean dictator Mobutu Sese Seko and has not had any request from the ousted strongman for a visa, head of government Mario Frick said on Sunday.
"It is not the wish of our government to take in Mr Mobutu," Frick told Reuters by telephone from the tiny principality nestled between Switzerland and Austria.
Mobutu flew into exile in Morocco after rebel forces took over his capital on Saturday and their leader Laurent Kabila proclaimed himself head of state.
Frick said he had made checks after French news reports speculated the Zairean ex-ruler could travel on to Liechtenstein to wait out French elections before seeking exile in France.
"I don't see any reason why we should take Mobutu in. We have no special relationship with him or with Zaire," Frick said, adding Mobutu did not own any property in Liechtenstein.
"We have had no official contact or unofficial contact (from Mobutu)," Frick said.
Neighbouring Switzerland, which has the closest international airport to Liechtenstein at Zurich, said on Saturday it would most likely reject any visa request from Mobutu.
